name: US Sports News
tagline: Scores, standings and the stories fans are searching for.

articles.title: Wembanyama Drops Career-Best 52 Points and 24 Rebounds as Spurs Edge Mavericks 112-111
articles.description: Victor Wembanyama scored a career-high 52 points with a career-best 24 rebounds, hitting the winning free throw with 24.2 seconds left as San Antonio beat Dallas 112-111 for a sixth straight win on Wednesday, November 4.
articles.sources: Reuters, November 5, 2026; Philstar/AFP, November 5, 2026
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama delivered the biggest night of his young career on Wednesday, November 4, scoring a career-best 52 points and grabbing a career-high 24 rebounds as the San Antonio Spurs outlasted the Dallas Mavericks 112-111, Reuters reported.

Wembanyama sank the winning free throw with 24.2 seconds left for the last of his 52 points, capping a night in which he also blocked eight shots, according to game reports. The win was San Antonio's sixth in a row, and it came the hard way: the Spurs led by 19 points early in the third quarter before Dallas fought back to take a 103-100 lead on a P.J. Washington three-pointer with 5:38 to play.

The rest of Wednesday's 14-game slate

The night's other heavyweight clash went to Philadelphia. Jaylen Brown scored 30 points and Joel Embiid added 26 as the 76ers beat the Detroit Pistons 112-106 in Detroit, moving to 8-1 at the top of the Eastern Conference standings, with Detroit falling to 6-2, Philstar reported. LeBron James added 13 points, 10 rebounds and eight assists for Philadelphia, while Tyrese Maxey hit three three-pointers.

Elsewhere, the reigning champion New York Knicks scored their biggest win of the season, routing the Chicago Bulls 135-105 at Madison Square Garden behind a 33-point night from Jalen Brunson, who made five three-pointers. In Los Angeles, Klay Thompson hit a game-winning three-pointer with one second left in overtime as Miami rallied past the Clippers 117-116, with Bam Adebayo scoring a season-high 35 points and 10 rebounds. Luka Doncic scored 40 points with nine rebounds and seven assists as the Lakers beat Sacramento 116-103, improving to 7-2 while the Kings fell to 1-7.

What the night means

The results tightened the early-season picture in both conferences. Philadelphia and San Antonio now look like the form teams of the opening weeks, with the 76ers' depth and the Spurs' superstar carrying them through close games. For Dallas, the loss was a reminder of how fine the margins are: a 19-point deficit erased, a lead taken late, and still a one-point defeat on the road. The NBA season continues on Thursday with a fresh slate, and Wembanyama's 52-and-24 line will take some beating as the individual performance of the season so far.

articles.title: Miami Tops First College Football Playoff Rankings, Followed by Georgia, Utah and Indiana
articles.description: The College Football Playoff selection committee released its first rankings on Tuesday, November 3, with undefeated Miami No. 1 ahead of Georgia, Utah and defending champion Indiana, while Ohio State debuted at No. 12.
articles.sources: NCAA.com, November 4, 2026; USA Today, November 3, 2026; Yardbarker, November 3, 2026
articles.body:
The College Football Playoff selection committee released its first rankings of the 2026 season on Tuesday, November 3, and as widely expected, undefeated Miami (8-0) sits at No. 1, NCAA.com reported.

The Hurricanes are followed by Georgia (7-1) at No. 2, undefeated Utah (8-0) at No. 3 and defending national champion Indiana (8-1) at No. 4. Under the current bracket, those four teams would earn first-round byes. Alabama (6-2) is fifth, Kentucky (7-1) sixth, Texas (6-2) seventh and undefeated UCLA (8-0) eighth, with BYU (7-1) ninth and Ole Miss (6-2) tenth.

Notre Dame and Ohio State on the outside looking in

The most debated placements came just outside the top ten. Notre Dame (7-1) sits at No. 11, well below its No. 4 position in the Associated Press poll, while Ohio State (6-2) debuted at No. 12 after its 30-18 loss at USC. Tennessee (6-2) is 13th, LSU (6-2) 14th and Texas Tech (7-1) 15th, with Boise State (7-1) rounding out the top 25 at No. 25. The committee's rankings are its own judgment, not a copy of the polls, and the gap between the two lists for Notre Dame and Ohio State is the clearest sign of that.

What happens next

The rankings are only the first of six weekly reveals. The committee will update its top 25 every Tuesday, with the next release on November 10 and the final bracket announced on Selection Day, Sunday, December 6. The playoff itself begins with four first-round campus games on December 18 and 19, and the national championship is scheduled for January 25 in Las Vegas.

The next shake-up could come within days: No. 1 Miami visits No. 11 Notre Dame on Saturday, a game that could reorder the top of the bracket immediately, and five top-25 matchups are scheduled for the weekend. For now, though, the Hurricanes — led by quarterback Darian Mensah and wide receiver Malachi Toney, according to USA Today — hold the top spot they were projected to take, and the committee has given the rest of the field five weeks to catch them.

articles.title: NBA Wednesday: 14 Games Return After Election Day, Led by 76ers at Pistons on ESPN
articles.description: The NBA returns from its Election Day break with 14 games on Wednesday, November 4, headlined by the 7-1 76ers at the 6-1 Pistons on ESPN and Mavericks at Spurs in the late ESPN slot.
articles.sources: NBA schedules via FantasyPros, Odyn, West 42 Sports, November 4, 2026
articles.body:
The NBA returns in full force on Wednesday, November 4, after going dark for Election Day, with a 14-game slate tipping off at 7 p.m. ET, schedules showed.

The headline games

The night opens with the Philadelphia 76ers (7-1) at the Detroit Pistons (6-1) at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN, a meeting of two of the East's early pacesetters, alongside Atlanta at Washington. The late ESPN game sends Dallas (4-3) to San Antonio (5-2) at 9:30 p.m. ET, while the Los Angeles Lakers (6-2) visit the Sacramento Kings (1-6) at 10 p.m. ET and Miami (2-5) visits the LA Clippers (1-6) at 10:30 p.m. ET.

The rest of the slate

Elsewhere, Milwaukee (1-6) visits Boston (5-2), Chicago (1-6) visits New York (3-4), Indiana (2-6) visits Memphis (6-1), Utah (1-6) visits New Orleans (3-4), Cleveland (4-3) visits Oklahoma City (5-2), Minnesota (5-3) visits Houston (7-1), Toronto (4-3) visits Denver (3-3), Portland (5-1) visits Phoenix (1-4), and Charlotte (3-5) visits Brooklyn (1-6). No results from Wednesday's games were available at the time of writing; this preview is based on the published schedule and records entering the night.

articles.title: Grizzlies Look to Rebound From First Loss as Pacers Visit Memphis
articles.description: Memphis, the NBA's last unbeaten team until Monday's overtime loss to New Orleans, hosts Indiana on Wednesday, with the Pacers on a five-game losing streak but coming off a near-miss against Atlanta.
articles.sources: Reuters, November 4, 2026
articles.body:
The Memphis Grizzlies will attempt to bounce back from their first loss of the season when they host the Indiana Pacers on Wednesday night, Reuters reported.

How Memphis lost

Memphis was the NBA's last unbeaten team before falling 135-134 in overtime to the visiting New Orleans Pelicans on Monday. Trailing by nine points with two minutes left, the Grizzlies relied on starting point guard Ty Jerome, who scored nine straight points to force overtime and finished with 40 points, his second game this season with 40 or more — but his potential game-winning shot in the closing seconds of overtime fell short. Memphis was attempting to start a season 7-0 for the first time.

A wounded Pacers side

Indiana has lost five straight games, but nearly overcame an exceptionally short-handed roster to earn a home win over Atlanta on Monday, falling 108-104 after Quenton Jackson's go-ahead three-point attempt with 43 seconds left missed. Indiana outscored Atlanta 48-40 in the second half of that game. Memphis enters at 6-1 and is favoured at home; the result had not been played at the time of writing.

articles.title: NBA Monday: Pelicans Hand Grizzlies First Loss in OT, Knicks Roll Past Nets
articles.description: New Orleans outlasted Memphis 135-134 in overtime to end the Grizzlies' 6-0 start, the Knicks beat the Nets for a 15th straight time, and Luka Doncic scored 42 as the Lakers beat Miami, in Monday's NBA roundup.
articles.sources: Reuters, November 3, 2026
articles.body:
Monday, November 2 delivered a full NBA slate — the last before the league goes dark for Election Day — with an overtime thriller in Memphis, a one-sided New York derby, and big scoring nights in Los Angeles and Oklahoma City, Reuters reported.

Pelicans end Memphis' perfect start

Zion Williamson scored 25 points and grabbed 11 rebounds, and Jeremiah Fears sank two clutch free throws with 7.3 seconds left in overtime as New Orleans beat host Memphis 135-134, handing the Grizzlies their first loss of the season and ending a franchise-record-matching six-game winning streak to open the campaign. Ty Jerome scored the last nine points of regulation to force overtime and finished with 40 points, but missed a 15-foot attempt for the win. New Orleans won its third straight after opening 0-4. Elsewhere, Sacramento beat Dallas 115-100 for its first win of the season, behind Darius Acuff Jr.'s 25 points.

Knicks, Lakers and Thunder win

The New York Knicks beat the Brooklyn Nets 103-90, extending their winning streak against their city rival to 15 games, with Landry Shamet scoring a season-high 22 points off the bench. Luka Doncic scored 42 points with 13 assists as the Lakers beat Miami 138-117, topping 40 points for the fourth time this season. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander scored a season-high 43 points, including the go-ahead three-pointer with 33 seconds left, as Oklahoma City edged Cleveland 117-112.

articles.title: Why There Are No NBA Games Today: The League Goes Dark for Election Day
articles.description: The NBA scheduled no games on Tuesday, November 3, for the fourth time in five years, so players, staff and fans can vote in the midterm elections — with all 15 teams having worn 'VOTE' shirts on Monday.
articles.sources: USA Today, November 3, 2026
articles.body:
There are no NBA games on Tuesday, November 3 — not because of a scheduling gap, but by design. For the fourth time in five years, the league has gone dark on Election Day to encourage voting, USA Today reported.

A deliberate blank date

The league did not schedule any games on Tuesday because the first polls close on the East Coast at 6 p.m. ET, with many more at 7 p.m. ET, and holding games would interfere with the ability of people who vote in person to do so, USA Today reported. It is one of only three days the NBA typically avoids scheduling games, alongside Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve. The league first began the Election Day initiative in November 2022 and also went dark on Election Day in 2023 and 2024.

Monday's message, Wednesday's return

On Monday, November 2, each team played, and at each of the 15 games players wore T-shirts that said 'VOTE' across the chest. Golden State coach Steve Kerr spoke before his team's game against Phoenix about the importance of voting. The NBA has also published voting resources for fans, including polling-site information and a voter-registration check. The league returns in full force on Wednesday, November 4, with a slate of 14 games.

articles.title: NFL Week 8: Bills Rout Ravens 36-10, Broncos Edge Chiefs 28-24 in Comeback
articles.description: Buffalo routed Baltimore 36-10 as Lamar Jackson left with a thumb injury, Denver came back from 24-13 down to beat Kansas City 28-24, and Cincinnati and Arizona won overtime thrillers on Sunday, November 1.
articles.sources: Field Level Media via Northland News Radio, WDRC, November 2, 2026
articles.body:
Sunday, November 1 delivered a full day of Week 8 drama, with Buffalo handing Baltimore a lopsided defeat, Denver taking over first place in the AFC West, and two overtime thrillers, recaps reported on November 2.

Bills dominate, Ravens lose both quarterbacks

Josh Allen threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns and set the franchise record for career touchdown passes as the Bills (6-1) beat the Ravens 36-10 in Orchard Park, holding Baltimore to 144 yards of total offense. Baltimore (4-4) lost Lamar Jackson to a right thumb injury on the opening play and backup Tyler Huntley to a right toe injury in the first half; Jackson was later placed on injured reserve, according to Field Level Media. Allen also rushed for a score in Buffalo's third straight win.

Broncos rally, Bengals and Cardinals win in OT

Denver (6-2) overcame a 24-13 deficit to beat Kansas City 28-24, with Jonah Coleman scoring the go-ahead touchdown with 1:56 remaining and a goal-line stand in the final seconds — Malcolm Roach sacking Patrick Mahomes, who threw for 321 yards and three touchdowns, to end it. Cincinnati beat Tennessee 43-36 in overtime behind Joe Burrow's five touchdown passes and game-winning rushing score, while Arizona rallied from 17-3 down to beat Dallas 33-30 in overtime. Washington also beat Philadelphia after erasing an early 10-0 deficit, handing the Eagles a sixth straight loss.

articles.title: First College Football Playoff Rankings Tuesday: Miami Projected No. 1, Ohio State on the Bubble
articles.description: The first College Football Playoff rankings arrive Tuesday, November 3 at 7 p.m. ET, with Miami projected No. 1 and two-loss Ohio State's fate — after its 30-18 loss at USC — the biggest question.
articles.sources: USA TODAY, Bleacher Report, NCAA.com, Athlon Sports, November 1-2, 2026
articles.body:
The first College Football Playoff rankings of the 2026 season will be unveiled on Tuesday, November 3, starting at 7 p.m. ET on ESPN, after a chaotic Week 9 that saw seven ranked teams fall.

The projected top

USA TODAY's projections put undefeated Miami (8-0) first, followed by Georgia (7-1), Utah (8-0), Indiana and UCLA, while Bleacher Report's top 25 also has Miami first ahead of Georgia, Utah, Indiana and UCLA, with Notre Dame and BYU in the mix. Miami survived a scare at North Carolina 38-35, Georgia dominated Florida 27-8, and Utah beat Cincinnati 49-25. The committee's top 25 will be revealed in parts through the one-hour show.

Ohio State's dilemma

Ohio State (6-2) fell 30-18 at USC in its first game without injured quarterback Julian Sayin, with true freshman Luke Fahey stepping in. Projections differ sharply on the Buckeyes: USA TODAY keeps them sixth, NCAA.com's prediction drops them to 11th, and Bleacher Report drops them to 13th — but all agree they have no margin for error left. Miami's next test comes quickly: the Hurricanes travel to Notre Dame in Week 10, a game that could shake up the bracket again within days.

articles.title: USC Stuns No. 2 Ohio State 30-18 as Seven Ranked Teams Fall in College Football's Wild Week 9
articles.description: Southern California beat No. 2 Ohio State 30-18 on a Halloween Saturday that saw seven ranked teams lose, shaking up the race ahead of Tuesday's first College Football Playoff rankings.
articles.sources: NCAA.com, PFF, Bleacher Report via Eastern Herald, November 1, 2026
articles.body:
It was a spooky Halloween in Week 9 of college football, with seven ranked teams falling throughout the day, NCAA.com reported on November 1 — headlined by Southern California's stunning 30-18 win over No. 2 Ohio State.

The upset of the day

USC earned a 30-18 victory over Ohio State in Los Angeles, handing the Buckeyes their first Big Ten loss of the season. The Trojans scored twice in the first quarter and kept Ohio State out of the end zone until late in the fourth, despite allowing 464 yards. Ohio State played with true freshman Luke Fahey in place of the injured Julian Sayin. Elsewhere, Iowa shut out No. 25 Wisconsin 30-0, Iowa State walked off No. 24 Oklahoma State 51-49, Oregon topped No. 20 Northwestern 34-26, Syracuse took down No. 19 SMU 30-27, No. 13 Texas Tech beat No. 22 Arizona 34-26, and No. 3 Georgia dominated No. 17 Florida 27-8.

What it means for the rankings

The chaos comes days before the first College Football Playoff rankings reveal on Tuesday, November 3, and with seven ranked teams falling there could be significant movement in the committee's top 25. Miami survived a scare at North Carolina 38-35 and Indiana needed overtime to beat Minnesota 23-16, while Texas beat Mississippi State 31-3 and Ole Miss routed Auburn 45-15. Bleacher Report's updated expert rankings, published November 1, dropped Ohio State from second to 13th and kept Miami first ahead of Georgia, Utah, Indiana and UCLA — an editorial ranking, not the committee's official list.

articles.title: NFL Sunday: Ravens-Bills and Chiefs-Broncos Headline a Packed Slate Capped by Eagles-Commanders
articles.description: Sunday's NFL slate features Ravens at Bills and Chiefs at Broncos among the afternoon games, closing with Eagles at Commanders on Sunday Night Football — with results still to come at writing time.
articles.sources: NFL schedule listings (Sync2Cal, SportsCal, Bookies), November 1, 2026
articles.body:
Sunday, November 1 brings a full NFL slate, headlined by a pair of heavyweight afternoon matchups and a primetime divisional clash to close the night, according to published schedules.

The afternoon headliners

The 1:00 p.m. ET window includes the Baltimore Ravens at the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium, the Dallas Cowboys hosting the Arizona Cardinals, the Detroit Lions hosting the Minnesota Vikings, and the Pittsburgh Steelers hosting the Cleveland Browns. The late afternoon brings the Los Angeles Rams against the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium and the Kansas City Chiefs at the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High, plus the New England Patriots at the Miami Dolphins.

Sunday Night Football closes the day

The nightcap is the Philadelphia Eagles at the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium, kicking off at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. At the time of writing, none of Sunday's games had been played, so no results are reported here; readers should check the live scoreboard for final scores. The slate follows a Thursday night win for Green Bay over Carolina and a Saturday of college football chaos, keeping a crowded football weekend rolling into November.

articles.title: Cowboys-Eagles Draws 18.8 Million Viewers, More Than Double World Series Game 3
articles.description: Monday Night Football's Cowboys-Eagles game drew 18.8 million viewers, dwarfing the 8.33 million who watched World Series Game 3 between Milwaukee and Tampa Bay.
articles.sources: NBC Sports, Barrett Media, Archynetys, October 30-31, 2026
articles.body:
A regular-season NFL game has beaten baseball's championship showcase by a wide margin in the television ratings, renewing debate about how Major League Baseball schedules its World Series.

The numbers

The Week 7 Cowboys-Eagles game on Monday night, October 26, which Dallas won 38-21, attracted 18.8 million viewers, according to ESPN figures cited by NBC Sports. Game 3 of the World Series between the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays averaged 8.33 million viewers, making it the fourth-least-watched World Series game ever, behind only Game 3 in 2023, Game 4 in 2023 and Game 3 in 2020.

The gap is striking because the World Series audience was respectable before the NFL arrived: Game 1 between Milwaukee and Tampa Bay averaged 12.26 million viewers and Game 2 drew 10.85 million, trailing last year's Dodgers-Blue Jays audiences by only a modest margin despite the absence of Shohei Ohtani, baseball's biggest television draw.

A scheduling debate, revived

There was once a time when the NFL went out of its way to avoid the World Series — in the 1970s it moved Monday Night Football to Thursday to dodge baseball's championship, and before 2010 it avoided Sunday night games during the Series. Commentators now argue the tables have turned, and that baseball should schedule World Series games on nights when NFL games are not being aired. The Cowboys' win also put Dallas back in the NFC East scramble, with upcoming matchups now carrying a defensive focus against the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.title: Brewers Celebrate First World Series Title With Victory Parade in Milwaukee
articles.description: The Milwaukee Brewers celebrated their first World Series championship with a victory parade in Milwaukee on October 30, two days after clinching the title at Tampa Bay.
articles.sources: Packers News, October 29-30, 2026
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers' championship week continued on Friday, October 30, with a victory parade in Milwaukee celebrating the club's first World Series title.

From Tampa Bay to Milwaukee

The Brewers clinched the title on October 28 at the Tampa Bay Rays, then made it back to Wisconsin in time to surprise fans at Lambeau Field on Thursday night, hoisting the Commissioner's Trophy while walking out of the tunnel between the first and second quarters of the Green Bay Packers' 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers. Several Brewers players took a Lambeau Leap, and the team watched the rest of the game from a private box wearing cheeseheads reading '2026 WS Champions'.

A Wisconsin celebration

The parade on Friday capped a week in which Wisconsin sport took center stage: a World Series title on Wednesday, a trophy cameo at Lambeau on Thursday, and a championship parade on Friday. The Packers, who beat Carolina 27-19 to move to 5-3, made sure the good vibes statewide kept rolling, closing out the Panthers in the fourth quarter after the Brewers' appearance had set the tone for the night.

articles.title: Packers Beat Panthers 27-19 on Thursday Night as Brewers Bring the World Series Trophy to Lambeau
articles.description: Green Bay beat Carolina 27-19 on Thursday Night Football, moving to 5-3, as Jordan Love threw for 288 yards and the Brewers paraded their new World Series trophy at Lambeau Field.
articles.sources: Sports Illustrated, October 30, 2026
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers beat the Carolina Panthers 27-19 on Thursday Night Football at Lambeau Field, moving to 5-3 and keeping pace in a crowded NFC North, a night after the Milwaukee Brewers captured their first World Series title.

How Green Bay won it

Jordan Love finished 30-of-41 for 288 yards with one touchdown and one interception. Emerging second-year wideout Matthew Golden caught seven passes for 79 yards and a touchdown, tight end Tucker Kraft added six catches for 53 yards and a touchdown, and workhorse running back Josh Jacobs scored twice, his second touchdown giving Green Bay a comfortable 27-10 advantage with 7:30 left in the third quarter.

It was not close to perfect for Green Bay. Downfield threat Christian Watson left in the first half and went to hospital to get his chest checked out, but eventually returned to the stadium to loud cheers from Packers fans — after catching eight passes for 113 yards, including a 53-yard reception that sparked the team in the first half. Carolina trimmed the deficit to eight points with 5:37 left in regulation on a 12-play, 70-yard touchdown drive, but could not complete the comeback.

A Wisconsin celebration

The night carried an extra Wisconsin flavor: members of the Brewers walked onto the field with the World Series trophy in hand for everyone in attendance, a day after Milwaukee's championship. The Packers, just like the Bears did on Thursday, have now also coughed up two first-round picks in a past blockbuster — theirs to acquire star edge rusher Micah Parsons from the Cowboys ahead of the 2025 season — and are a day closer to getting Parsons back on the field.

Green Bay now sits at 5-3, behind the 6-0 Vikings and ahead in a division where the Bears are 5-2 and the Lions 4-2. Carolina, which entered the night leading the NFC South despite its record, falls further into a fight it cannot afford to lose.

articles.title: Bears Go All-In: Chicago Lands Jeffery Simmons From Titans for Two First-Round Picks
articles.description: The Chicago Bears acquired All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans on October 29, sending two first-round picks plus a fourth-rounder in the NFL's loudest move of the season.
articles.sources: USA TODAY, NBC Sports, NDTV Sports, October 29-30, 2026
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears have gone all-in. On Thursday, October 29, the Bears agreed to acquire All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons from the Tennessee Titans, sending two first-round picks as part of a blockbuster package ahead of the November 10 trade deadline.

The terms of the deal

Chicago will send its first-round picks in 2027 and 2028, plus a fourth-round pick in 2027, to Tennessee in exchange for Simmons and a fifth-round pick in 2028, the teams confirmed. Simmons is the first defensive tackle in the common draft era, since 1967, to be swapped for multiple first-round picks.

Simmons, 29, was a first-round pick in 2019 and has spent his entire NFL career with Tennessee. He has 414 career tackles, 72 for losses, nine forced fumbles, 46.5 sacks and 96 quarterback hits in 106 regular-season games, and has four sacks and six tackles for loss in seven games this season. He signed a three-year extension in July worth a reported $105.8 million, keeping him under contract through 2030.

Why each side did it

The Bears, 5-2 and second in the NFC North, are clearly in pursuit of their first Lombardi Trophy since the famed 1985 team won it all. Titans coach Robert Saleh did not sugarcoat the short-term upshot, saying the trade “sucks” but was “necessary,” while general manager Mike Borgonzi said the team was not actively shopping Simmons until Bears general manager Ryan Poles reached out on Wednesday night.

For Tennessee, 1-6 and sitting near the top of the 2027 draft order, the deal banks two future first-rounders for a rebuild — though it costs the team its best player and sack leader. Simmons is reported to debut for Chicago on Monday night at Seattle, where the Bears will learn fast whether the price was worth it.

articles.title: Brewers Win First World Series Title in Franchise History, Beating Rays 4-1 in Game 5
articles.description: The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on October 28, clinching the first World Series championship in the franchise's 58-year history.
articles.sources: USA TODAY, NBC Sports, October 28-29, 2026
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are World Series champions for the first time. Milwaukee beat the Tampa Bay Rays 4-1 in Game 5 on Wednesday night, October 28, at Tropicana Field, capping a 4-1 series victory and ending a championship wait that stretched across the franchise's 58-year history.

How Game 5 was won

Second-year ace Jacob Misiorowski threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings of two-hit ball before leaving with a right calf cramp, departing with a 4-0 lead. Rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt drove in two runs and set a World Series rookie record with six consecutive hits across Games 4 and 5, while Jackson Chourio set a five-game Series record with 11 hits. The bullpen covered the final 4 1/3 innings without allowing a run, and Trevor Megill closed out the ninth after Tampa Bay finally scored.

A dominant October

The Brewers finished October 11-2, reeling off an eight-game winning streak that was only interrupted by Tampa Bay's 12-inning win in Game 4. The club won 114 games including the playoffs, and dethroned the two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers along the way. Misiorowski, who led the majors with 252 strikeouts and a 1.80 ERA in the regular season, won Games 1 and 5 of the Series.

Dedicated to Mr. Baseball

The title carried special meaning for a franchise shaped by broadcaster Bob Uecker, who died of cancer in January 2025 without seeing the Brewers crowned champions. Christian Yelich and manager Pat Murphy dedicated the win to Uecker after the final out, with Yelich saying he wished Uecker could have been there to see it. The club's only previous World Series trip, in 1982, ended in a Game 7 loss to St. Louis.

articles.title: Panthers vs. Packers on Thursday Night Football: Two Wounded Contenders Meet at Lambeau
articles.description: The Carolina Panthers visit the Green Bay Packers on Thursday Night Football tonight, with both teams coming off humbling losses and fighting for their playoff positioning.
articles.sources: NDTV Sports, USA TODAY Sportsbook Wire, Athlon Sports, October 29, 2026
articles.body:
Thursday Night Football heads to Lambeau Field tonight, where the Green Bay Packers host the Carolina Panthers at 8:15 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Both teams arrive wounded, both need a win, and the standings make the stakes stranger than the records suggest.

Two teams coming off bad losses

Green Bay is 4-3 and sits last in the NFC North after a 20-17 loss at Detroit on Sunday, despite quarterback Jordan Love throwing for 274 yards and two touchdowns. Carolina is 3-3 yet leads the NFC South, even after a 43-13 home loss to Tampa Bay in which Bryce Young threw for just 163 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions. Green Bay enters as a 3.5-point home favorite, and most national experts are picking the Packers — though nearly all see a close game.

Injuries shape the matchup

Carolina's offensive line is battered: Taylor Moton is out, Ikem Ekwonu is on the physically unable to perform list, and Jaelan Phillips is questionable, while Jonathon Brooks, Jaycee Horn and Xavier Legette are also sidelined. Green Bay has its own absences, with Jayden Reed and Javon Hargrave on injured reserve and Micah Parsons on the PUP list. The running game offers Green Bay a path: its ground attack ranks last in the league, but Carolina's run defense has been one of its weaknesses all season.

What a win changes

A Packers victory would lift Green Bay to 5-3 heading into a mini-bye week and keep pace in a crowded NFC North. A Panthers win would strengthen Carolina's grip on the NFC South and serve as a statement road victory for a young team. Kickoff is 8:15 p.m. ET, with pregame coverage from 7 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Rays Stun Brewers in 12th to Avoid Sweep and Force World Series Game 5
articles.description: Pinch hitter Ben Williamson's walk-off single in the 12th inning gave Tampa Bay a 4-3 win over Milwaukee in Game 4, keeping the Rays alive in the World Series.
articles.sources: USA TODAY, NBC Sports, Philstar/AFP, October 28, 2026
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Rays refused to be swept. Pinch hitter Ben Williamson delivered a walk-off single in the 12th inning on Tuesday night, completing a wild 4-3 comeback over the Milwaukee Brewers in Game 4 of the World Series at Tropicana Field and forcing a Game 5 on Wednesday.

How the 12th unfolded

Milwaukee looked set to celebrate its first World Series championship in 57 years when rookie shortstop Cooper Pratt, capping a four-hit night, homered to lead off the top of the 12th for a 3-2 lead. The champagne was reportedly ready and the plastic lining was being unrolled. Instead, the bottom of the inning unravelled for the Brewers: third baseman Joey Ortiz threw Junior Caminero's routine grounder past first base, Liam Hicks singled, Jonny DeLuca singled home the tying run, Chandler Simpson loaded the bases, and Williamson bounced a chopper into right field to score pinch runner Nick Fortes.

"Just shows the resiliency of this group," Williamson said afterwards. "We continue to fight and that's been the motto this series and this whole season." Ortiz was blunt about his error: "There's no excuse. Not one at all. I should make that play every time."

The Brewers still lead the best-of-seven series 3-1, and they will turn to ace Jacob Misiorowski in Game 5 on Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET in St. Petersburg. It was the fourth game in World Series history in which a team staved off elimination with an extra-inning victory. Tampa Bay needs three more.

articles.title: Caminero Says He'll Play Game 5 Despite Foot Injury: 'If My Foot Is Broken, I'll Play Tomorrow'
articles.description: Rays slugger Junior Caminero injured his left foot during the Game 4 rally but vowed to play in Wednesday's must-win Game 5 against Milwaukee.
articles.sources: NBC Sports/AP, October 28, 2026
articles.body:
All-Star slugger Junior Caminero injured his left foot during the Tampa Bay Rays' late rally in Game 4 of the World Series on Tuesday night, but he says he will play Wednesday in Game 5. Caminero began limping after reaching on Joey Ortiz's throwing error leading off the 12th inning, ran first-to-third on Liam Hicks' single, and was then replaced by pinch runner Cedric Mullins.

"If my foot is broken," Caminero said, "I'll play tomorrow." He did not reveal the extent of the injury, saying it did not matter with Tampa Bay on the brink of elimination.

Why the Rays need him

The 23-year-old hit 42 home runs with 101 RBIs while playing all 162 games in the regular season, but he has just one homer and five RBIs in 13 postseason games, and the Rays are hitting .195 with a single home run in the World Series. Manager Kevin Cash left no doubt about his plans: "He'll play tomorrow on one leg. I'll make sure of it." Game 5 is Wednesday at 8 p.m. ET at Tropicana Field, with Milwaukee's Jacob Misiorowski starting for the Brewers, who lead the series 3-1.

articles.title: Brewers Rout Rays 10-1 to Take Commanding 3-0 World Series Lead
articles.description: Milwaukee dismantled Tampa Bay 10-1 in Game 3 behind an eight-run fifth inning, moving one win from a World Series title and a first championship for the franchise.
articles.sources: Associated Press, Sarasota Herald-Tribune
articles.body:
Milwaukee moved to the brink of a World Series title on Monday night, dismantling Tampa Bay 10-1 in Game 3 behind an eight-run fifth inning and four hits from Jackson Chourio. The Brewers now lead the series 3-0, with Game 4 set for Tuesday night at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida.

Brice Turang and William Contreras each went 3 for 5 in the rout, as Milwaukee's lineup overwhelmed Tampa Bay pitching in the decisive fifth inning. The Rays managed just one run on three hits on the night, a continuation of an offensive drought that has defined the series so far.

One win from history

The Brewers are now one victory from a championship that would crown a first-time World Series winner, with both Milwaukee and Tampa Bay chasing the first title in franchise history. Milwaukee swept the Dodgers in the National League Championship Series to reach the Fall Classic, while Tampa Bay beat Cleveland in six games in the American League Championship Series. The Brewers finished the regular season 103-59, the best record in baseball, and have carried that dominance into October.

History favors Milwaukee heavily. Teams leading a World Series 3-0 have almost always gone on to win it, and the Rays now face the prospect of the first World Series sweep since 2012, when the San Francisco Giants finished off the Detroit Tigers. Tampa Bay had hoped the Tropicana Field crowd would spark a comeback, but the Game 3 blowout has left the home team searching for answers.

Game 4: elimination game for Tampa Bay

Game 4 starts at 8 p.m. ET on Tuesday and will be broadcast nationally on Fox, with Joe Davis and John Smoltz calling the game. Griffin Jax is scheduled to open the game on the mound for the Rays, who are in desperate need of offense after scratching together just one run in Game 3. Milwaukee has yet to announce its Game 4 starter, though Dustin May is reported as a likely candidate.

If the Rays win, Game 5 would follow on Wednesday at Tropicana Field. If Milwaukee completes the sweep, the celebration will begin on the road, capping a postseason run that has seen the Brewers lose just once in the National League Championship Series and dominate the World Series to date.

articles.title: Cowboys Crush Eagles 38-21 to Revive NFC East Hopes
articles.description: Dallas bounced back in the division race by beating Philadelphia 38-21 on Monday night, handing the defending champions their fifth straight loss behind three Dak Prescott touchdown passes.
articles.sources: BBC Sport, Sports Wire Live
articles.body:
Dallas bounced back in the NFC East race on Monday night, defeating Philadelphia 38-21 behind a stellar performance from CeeDee Lamb and Javonte Williams, who combined for 229 yards and three touchdowns. Quarterback Dak Prescott threw three touchdown passes as the Cowboys ended a two-game losing run and secured their first win at Philadelphia since 2021.

The victory lifted Dallas to 3-4 and kept its division hopes alive, while the Eagles fell to 2-5 after a fifth consecutive defeat. Philadelphia, which won the Super Bowl in 2025, has seen its season unravel since a 2-0 start, losing star quarterback Jalen Hurts to a potentially season-ending blood clot and struggling to stop the slide since.

A rivalry game that turned early

The Cowboys took control behind an efficient offense and a defense that kept Philadelphia from finding any sustained rhythm. Lamb and Williams did the damage on the ground and through the air, combining for 229 yards and three touchdowns, while Prescott's three scoring passes kept the Eagles chasing the game. Dallas closed out the win in front of a hostile Philadelphia crowd, a result that reshapes the early NFC East picture.

For the Eagles, the loss extends a miserable stretch that has seen the defending champions lose five straight. The absence of Hurts has loomed large, and the team has struggled to replace his production and leadership. BBC Sport's week-seven roundup noted that few would have predicted Philadelphia's collapse at the start of the season, given the roster that won the title last year.

Elsewhere in week seven

Week seven also saw the end of the season's last unbeaten runs in other games. Kansas City lost at defending champions Seattle, and San Francisco suffered its first defeat, leaving Minnesota as the league's only unbeaten team. The Chiefs' loss to Seattle came in a primetime matchup between the teams with the season's best offense and best defense by total yards, and it marked the return of Kenneth Walker, last season's Super Bowl Most Valuable Player, to Seattle after joining Kansas City in the off-season.

For Dallas, the win offers a path back into contention. The Cowboys still trail in the division, but with the Eagles reeling and the season not yet at its midpoint, Monday night's result keeps their hopes alive and sets up a crucial stretch of games in the weeks ahead.

articles.title: 2026 Sports Equinox: World Series, WNBA Finals and Monday Night Football Share One Night
articles.description: Monday, October 26 is the 2026 sports equinox, a rare night when the World Series, the WNBA Finals, Monday Night Football and regular-season NBA and NHL games all take place.
articles.sources: USA Today, Sports Wire Live
articles.body:
There might not be a better Monday on the sports calendar than October 26. It is officially the 2026 sports equinox, a rare convergence when the calendars of the biggest leagues in North America overlap to create a sports fan's dream night.

This year, the sports equinox features games in all five major professional leagues, plus championship action in two of them. That means the World Series, the WNBA Finals, Monday Night Football and regular-season NBA and NHL games are all on the schedule for the same evening.

World Series Game 3: Brewers at Rays

The headline baseball matchup is World Series Game 3, with the Milwaukee Brewers visiting the Tampa Bay Rays at 8 p.m. Eastern on FOX. Milwaukee has established a 2-0 lead in the series, with William Contreras and Sal Frelick playing key roles alongside reliever Aaron Ashby, so Tampa Bay faces a near must-win game on its home field.

A 3-0 series deficit has historically been almost impossible to overcome in the World Series, which gives Game 3 enormous stakes for the Rays and a chance for the Brewers to take a stranglehold on the championship.

WNBA Finals Game 5: Dream at Valkyries

At the same 8 p.m. Eastern hour, the WNBA Finals continue with Game 5, with the Atlanta Dream visiting the Golden State Valkyries. A Finals game this deep into a series is one of the most-watched spectacles in basketball, and the late-series stakes guarantee a charged atmosphere.

The game airs on USA Network, CNBC and Peacock, giving fans multiple ways to watch the championship showdown.

Monday Night Football: Cowboys at Eagles

The NFL contributes one of its fiercest rivalries: the Dallas Cowboys visit the Philadelphia Eagles at 8:15 p.m. Eastern on ESPN and ABC. Cowboys-Eagles games routinely draw some of the largest regular-season audiences of the year, and this one lands in the middle of a crowded championship night.

The matchup also carries divisional weight, with both teams fighting for position in the NFC East as the season enters its second half.

A full NBA and NHL slate

The NBA adds nine games to the night, including the Washington Wizards at Charlotte, the Chicago Bulls at Boston, Dallas at Miami, and a late showcase between the Golden State Warriors and the Denver Nuggets at 10 p.m. Eastern. Golden State arrives still searching for its first win of the season after an 0-3 start, while Denver sits at 1-1.

The NHL rounds out the equinox with its own slate of games, including the Kings against the Rangers. With five leagues and two championships sharing one night, October 26 is the kind of evening sports fans circle on the calendar years in advance, and the kind that only comes around when every league's schedule happens to align.

articles.title: Giants Edge Texans 27-21 in Overtime Behind McCarthy Debut and Skattebo's Return
articles.description: The New York Giants beat the Houston Texans 27-21 in overtime on Sunday, fueled by a strong debut from J.J. McCarthy and a bounce-back rushing day from Cam Skattebo.
articles.sources: Sports Wire Live, Athlon Sports
articles.body:
The New York Giants secured a 27-21 overtime victory against the Houston Texans on Sunday, fueled by a strong debut from J.J. McCarthy and a bounce-back rushing performance by Cam Skattebo.

The win counts among the biggest of Week 7 for the Giants, who found a way to close out a tight game in the extra period after a back-and-forth afternoon. McCarthy's debut gave the offense a spark, while Skattebo's physical running set the tone on the ground.

Skattebo's defiant message after rare penalty

The game's most talked-about moment may have come away from the scoreboard. Skattebo was flagged for unnecessary roughness in the first quarter after lowering his helmet into Texans safety M.J. Stewart during a run, a rare call against an offensive player.

Entering Week 7, only four lowering-the-helmet penalties had been called across the NFL this season, with just one assessed against an offensive player, Texans tight end Foster Moreau. Skattebo made it clear after the game that he has no plans to change his physical running style, even if the league keeps penalizing or fining him for it.

As reported by Athlon Sports, Skattebo said the NFL loves to post him when he does things like that but then also wants to take things from him, adding that he will run the ball the way he wants to run it, and if he keeps getting flags or fines, he guesses he will play for free.

A fine already on the books

The penalty was not Skattebo's first brush with the league's helmet rules. The NFL fined him $7,073 on October 2 for impermissible helmet use in a Week 3 win over the Tennessee Titans, so Sunday's flag puts him squarely back in the league's spotlight.

Whether a further fine follows is now a talking point around the league. Players around the NFL will be watching closely, since enforcement of the lowering-the-helmet rule against ball carriers has been inconsistent, and Skattebo's case has become the most visible test of it this season.

What the win means

For the Giants, the overtime win is a building block. A debut at quarterback that produces points, a running game that imposes its will, and a defense that holds up in overtime are the ingredients of a team finding its identity midseason.

For Houston, the loss stings, especially one decided in overtime after the Texans had chances to close it out. The Texans now regroup with the same questions every close-loss team faces: how to finish games, and how to handle a Giants team that refused to go away.

Week 7's other big storyline, the Seattle Seahawks' 20-3 win over the previously unbeaten Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football, only adds to a weekend that reshaped the early playoff picture. The Giants, for their part, will take the win and the headlines, and Skattebo will take his running style with him into next week, fines or not.

articles.title: Unbeaten 76ers Host Unbeaten Pistons in Early-Season Eastern Showdown
articles.description: Philadelphia entered Sunday 3–0 and Detroit 2–0, with both teams living up to preseason contender billing — and both managing key absences for the Oct. 25 clash.
articles.sources: Reuters, Bleacher Nation, NBC Sports Philadelphia, Detroit Free Press
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers and Detroit Pistons arrived at their Sunday, October 25, 2026 meeting as the Eastern Conference's early-season surprise package: two unbeaten teams, both expected to contend, meeting in Philadelphia at Xfinity Mobile Arena. The 76ers were 3–0 with a new star-studded lineup; the Pistons were 2–0 after finishing with the best record in the East last season.

Philadelphia's start had already produced drama. The new lineup debuted with a road win over the defending champion New York Knicks, followed that up with a 29-point comeback victory over the Cleveland Cavaliers, and most recently topped the Milwaukee Bucks 127–116 on Saturday behind Joel Embiid's 10th career triple-double — 28 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists — while Jaylen Brown added 27 points and Tyrese Maxey chipped in with 26.

A test of depth on both sides

The matchup was shaped as much by who would miss it as by who would play. Embiid was expected to rest on the second night of a back-to-back, which could mean a bigger offensive role for VJ Edgecombe, who scored a season-high 17 points on Saturday, and sixth man Kentavious Caldwell-Pope. Detroit, meanwhile, ruled out Jalen Duren with a right hamstring strain and listed Ausar Thompson as questionable after he sprained his right ankle in Friday's 128–111 win over Miami.

Detroit's early wins had quality: a season-opening 121–113 victory over the Boston Celtics on October 20, in which Duren posted 22 points and nine rebounds, and the rout of the Heat. Philadelphia's slow starts were the one concern — the Sixers trailed Cleveland by 24 points at halftime and held only a one-point lead over winless Milwaukee late in the first half before Maxey banked in a half-court shot at the buzzer.

What it means — and what it doesn't

Jaylen Brown kept the perspective blunt after the Bucks win: “We can't be satisfied being 3–0. We can't be satisfied with where we're at right now. We're building for something, so we've got to get better.” Coach Nick Nurse agreed it was early: “As we're going here, it's still really early for us. ... We're trying to learn things that we're going to polish quick.” One October Sunday does not decide a conference — but for two unbeaten teams, it was the first real measuring stick of the season.

Detroit's depth was already being tested before tip-off. Ron Holland, now in his third season, had a productive game on Friday with eight points, five rebounds, four assists, a steal and zero turnovers in 22 minutes, and the Pistons picked up his fourth-year rookie option on Monday, according to the Detroit Free Press. Kevin Huerter was also among the wings in line to start in Thompson's absence. For Philadelphia, the absence of Embiid opened a different kind of test: whether a team built around its star center could keep its offense humming with LeBron James initiating more of the attack, a look coach Nick Nurse said the Sixers had already tried in stretches — including a brief shift at center during the season-opening win over the Knicks.

articles.title: Hornets 115–110 Heat: Miller's 34 Drops Miami to 0–3
articles.description: Brandon Miller bounced back from one of the worst nights in Hornets history to score 34, as Charlotte held off a late Miami rally and left the star-studded Heat winless.
articles.sources: Associated Press via theScore, Heavy, Sports Illustrated
articles.body:
Brandon Miller scored 34 points and the Charlotte Hornets beat the winless Miami Heat 115–110 on Saturday, October 24, 2026, bouncing back from one of the worst losses in franchise history a night earlier. The win moved Charlotte to 2–1; the loss dropped Miami, which added superstar forward Giannis Antetokounmpo during the summer, to 0–3.

The turnaround was personal for Miller. Charlotte's 128–81 loss to Atlanta on Friday in its home opener was the fifth-largest in franchise history, and Miller missed 12 of 14 field goal attempts and 10 of his 11 three-point tries in a six-point effort that came four days after he signed a five-year, $209 million contract extension. On Saturday he delivered a game-high 34 points with seven rebounds and four assists. Dennis Schroder added 25 points, Naz Reid had 23 and Grayson Allen 20 for Charlotte.

A third-quarter surge, then a Miami rally

Charlotte, which was 11 of 51 from three-point range on Friday, made 16 of 43 on Saturday. Five of those threes sparked a 24–7 run in the third quarter that turned a 68–63 lead into a 92–70 advantage with 2:55 left in the quarter, to the delight of the sellout crowd of 19,611 at Spectrum Center. But Miami refused to go away: with Antetokounmpo in foul trouble — he would foul out with 1:57 to play — coach Erik Spoelstra's rally forged ties at 100, 102 and 104.

After the final tie with 3:46 to play, Allen turned the momentum back Charlotte's way for good with an acrobatic three-pointer from the left wing while being fouled by Tim Hardaway Jr. at the end of the 24-second shot clock. Antetokounmpo was limited to 14 points — more than 20 fewer than the 35.5 per game he averaged in his first two games after his trade from the Milwaukee Bucks — while Davion Mitchell led Miami with 22 points and 10 assists.

Spoelstra's challenge

After the game, Spoelstra sent a clear message to his stuttering roster: “We just have to find a way. That's what it is right now. We have to be able to sustain that level of effort and focus and discipline for 48 minutes.” He added: “Our system is our system. We can be that active at any point during the game. When we aren't we are choosing not to and paying the price right now.” It is, per ESPN Research as cited by the Daily Caller, the first 0–3 start of Spoelstra's 19 years as Miami's head coach. Three games is far too early to panic — but for a team built to contend now, it is also far too early to look this lost.

articles.title: College Football Week 8: UCF Stuns No. 2 BYU, Texas Survives Ole Miss, Virginia Tech Wins at Clemson
articles.description: Week 8 delivered upsets everywhere: UCF beat No. 2 BYU in double overtime, Indiana survived Michigan 13–6 in overtime, and Virginia Tech won 20–16 at Clemson on a late fourth-down touchdown.
articles.sources: The Football Corner, Detroit Free Press, Sportradar, Deadspin, USA Today Clemson Wire
articles.body:
Week 8 of the 2026 college football season, played Saturday, October 24, was one of the wildest weekends of the year — and the Big 12's playoff picture descended into chaos. Texas survived Ole Miss 34–27 after blowing a 21-point lead, UCF stunned No. 2 BYU in double overtime following one of the strangest endings imaginable, and South Carolina walked off Tennessee, according to The Football Corner's weekend recap.

In the Big Ten, No. 6 Indiana went on the road and survived a stiff test from Michigan in a 13–6 overtime victory in Wolverines freshman quarterback Tommy Carr's first career start. It was Indiana's first win at Michigan since 1967, and the Hoosiers won despite a subpar day from a banged-up Josh Hoover, who completed only eight of 18 passes for 81 yards, no touchdowns and an interception. Elsewhere in the conference, Minnesota walked off No. 14 Iowa 13–10, Wisconsin beat No. 15 USC 24–7, and Illinois beat No. 25 Oregon 21–10.

Virginia Tech's late stunner at Clemson

The nightcap produced another upset. Ethan Grunkemeyer threw two touchdown passes, including the game-winner with 1:44 left, as visiting Virginia Tech slipped past Clemson 20–16 in an Atlantic Coast Conference defensive struggle at Memorial Stadium. Both of Grunkemeyer's scoring passes went to Luke Reynolds, and the go-ahead score came on a fourth-and-1 play from the Clemson 5, when Grunkemeyer lobbed a pass to Reynolds, alone in the back of the end zone.

Clemson had reeled off 13 straight points in the third quarter to take a 16–10 lead, but the Hokies responded with the game's final 10 points. Grunkemeyer completed 20 of 32 passes for 156 yards with no interceptions, while Clemson freshman quarterback Tait Reynolds completed 20 of 26 passes for 153 yards and ran for 63 yards and a touchdown. The win was Virginia Tech's second straight after its first two losses under first-year coach James Franklin, and its first win at Clemson since 2007.

What the weekend changed

The results reshuffled the polls: Miami stayed No. 1 in the coaches poll, with Ohio State, Georgia, Indiana and Utah rounding out the top five, while BYU fell to No. 9 and Alabama — which rallied past Texas A&M — climbed to No. 10. Cincinnati took down Texas Tech, LSU crushed Auburn, and UCLA kept its unbeaten record intact with a 28–10 victory against Michigan State. With the season now past its midpoint, Week 8 was a reminder that no lead, no ranking and no home field is safe — and that the playoff race is only getting stranger.
